title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is typed and photographed upside down. It is headed 'NA 20' and is not mathematical working. It is a set of addenda, dated 6 May 1986, to footnotes on pages 951–953 of Récoltes et Semailles (the 'Enterrement' part, which deals with the Mebkhout / Riemann–Hilbert affair). It does not belong to the Boolean-algebra and lattice calculations on the neighbouring pages.

The mathematical object is the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence in derived form. For a complex manifold X there are two functors:
- m: from the derived category of regular holonomic D_X-modules to the derived category of constructible sheaves (the de Rham or solutions functor);
- M: going back the other way.
The correspondence is that these are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences, with the constructible side corresponding to the perverse t-structure.

Grothendieck revises his earlier account in R&S, which had relied on Mebkhout's version of events:
1. He now has 'no doubt' that the idea of the functors m and M in the derived-category setting is due to Kashiwara.
2. The relevant conjecture is mentioned as early as January 1978 in a text by Ramis, who attributes it to Kashiwara.
3. Until about September 1979 the conjecture was regarded by those who had heard of it, Kashiwara and Mebkhout included, as a mathematical curiosity of little consequence.
4. He now strongly doubts that Mebkhout had, before late 1979 or during 1980, the intuition of the equivalence's crucial role in a new 'theory of coefficients'.
5. He qualifies his term 'foncteur de Mebkhout' and suggests 'foncteur de Kashiwara–Mebkhout'. The reason given is Mebkhout's important role in making the functor's importance understood, notably through his duality philosophy.
6. The first fragment records that the person behind the 'foncteur de Mebkhout' terminology in the conjecture (most likely Mebkhout) assured him of his entire good faith. That person claimed not to have known of the appendix to Ramis's exposé until Grothendieck passed on Schapira's letter about it in January 1986.

No mathematical argument is developed on the page.
errors: Not a mathematical error but a historical self-correction. The page retracts or qualifies the attribution of the derived Riemann–Hilbert functors given in the main text of Récoltes et Semailles (main text sole-credits Mebkhout; the page assigns the idea to Kashiwara, with Mebkhout in an important role).

ideas.what: Derived-category Riemann–Hilbert correspondence between regular holonomic D-modules and constructible sheaves, via functors m and M.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kashiwara (conjectured in the 1970s, proved 1980/84) and Mebkhout (1980/84), independently
ideas.where_published: Récoltes et Semailles, L'Enterrement (Mebkhout notes); the 6 May 1986 addenda are possibly in later circulated/published versions — unsure

ideas.what: Historical attribution: the conjecture appears in a January 1978 text by Ramis crediting Kashiwara, and its importance was unrecognised until about September 1979.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed in literature on the R&S controversy (e.g. Kashiwara–Schapira commentaries)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the addenda to Récoltes et Semailles

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed addendum to Récoltes et Semailles in which Grothendieck himself retracts the Mebkhout-centred priority story and credits Kashiwara. That is historically interesting as a self-correction. However, the Kashiwara/Mebkhout priority question is well documented, and the page contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; it is a typed sheet, 'NA 20'.
'figurant dans le conjecture' should read 'figurant dans la conjecture' (or is a typing slip in the original).
'[-Mebkhout apparemment ...-]' and the following struck-through text are typed overstrikes (x-ed out). They are mostly illegible and correctly omitted.
'avec un grain [?] de sel' — the reading 'grain de sel' is clear.
'vu le rôle important [-principal-]': the line reads 'tant principal joué'. The word 'principal' appears typed over or x-ed and replaced; the intended reading is 'rôle important joué par Mebkhout'.
The last line ends 'que pour le [x-ed out word]'; the sentence continues on another sheet.
